transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… my regular doctor asked me to come in. She’s been concerned because my weight’s gotten pretty low, and I guess people around me are making a bigger deal of it than I expected.

I don’t feel like it’s all bad, honestly. Being lighter sort of helps me move around the shop easier, keeps me from feeling slowed down when I’m working. But… I’m here because she thought I should talk to someone, so I’m trying to do the right thing.
Have you been intentionally trying to lose weight, or has this happened without you actively trying?

I mean… I wouldn’t say I’m trying to do anything drastic. It’s more that on days I’m in the workshop, I get into a rhythm and I don’t really want to stop for a proper meal. I’ll usually just have tea, maybe a few careful bites of something.

It feels like stopping for a real lunch throws off the control I have over the day, if that makes sense. I know that probably sounds… not ideal. But it doesn’t feel like I’m forcing it exactly.
Do you feel distressed about your weight or the way you eat, or have you noticed it affecting your daily life in ways that bother you?

I wouldn’t say I’m distressed exactly… I mean, I still get myself to the shop and I’m working. So in that sense I’m managing, I think.

But… I guess it has changed things some. My husband and the apprentices have started stepping in more with the heavier work, and they check on me more than they used to. I know they mean well, and I don’t want to sound ungrateful, but it makes the shop feel a little less like it’s mine, if that makes sense. Like I’m being watched instead of just trusted to do my work.
Have you noticed any concern about gaining weight or do you go out of your way to avoid eating certain foods or meals?

I… I suppose I do watch that more than I probably should. I don’t mean to be difficult about food, but if something feels heavy, or if it’s the kind of rich food we used to have around the holidays, I get nervous almost right away.

It’s like I start thinking if I let myself have that, I’ll gain weight and lose the grip I’ve worked hard to keep. I know that may not sound very reasonable… but yes, I do avoid those things.
Do you ever make yourself sick or exercise more than usual after eating to try to control your weight?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I don’t make myself sick, and I wouldn’t say I exercise to make up for eating.

I’m on my feet in the shop, of course, and some days are more physical than others, but that’s just the work. I’m not… going out afterward to punish myself or anything like that. Is that what you mean?
Can you tell me about your weight or how much you weigh now compared to what you think is normal for someone your height and age?

Well… I don’t know if I should put it this way, but my doctor was concerned enough to send me here because my weight’s gotten very low. Everyone’s been making quite a fuss about it.

I know for my height and age it’s probably less than what they’d call normal, but… I don’t feel as bad about it as everyone else seems to. Part of me feels like being lighter helps me move around the shop more easily, like I’m not slowed down. I know that may not be the right way to think about it, but that’s how it feels to me.
Do you see your weight as too low, or do you feel like others are misunderstanding or exaggerating how serious this is?

I… I don’t really see it the way everyone else does, if I’m honest. My husband says I look too thin, and even the apprentices at the shop have made comments, which is a bit embarrassing.

But I keep telling them I’m fine. I feel like they’re making it sound worse than it is, you know? Like they’re confusing being disciplined with being sick. I don’t want to ignore what you’re saying, of course… I just don’t feel as alarmed about it as they seem to.
Do you feel like you are overweight or see parts of your body as too big, even if others say you're too thin?

I’m not sure I’d say I feel overweight, no. That sounds… a bit extreme. I don’t look in the mirror and think, “I’m huge,” or anything like that.

There are bits I fuss over, maybe, like anyone does, but I know people are telling me I’m thin. I suppose I don’t always see what they’re seeing, if that makes sense. But I wouldn’t want to exaggerate it or say something that isn’t true.
Do you ever look in the mirror and feel like you still appear heavier than you actually are, even though others tell you that you're too thin?

I’m not sure… I don’t think I’d put it exactly that way. I don’t usually stand there thinking I look heavy, no.

Sometimes I look and think something doesn’t look quite right, or I fuss over how my clothes sit, but if people are telling me I’m too thin, I understand that’s what they’re seeing. I suppose I just don’t always feel it the same way. Does that make sense?
Have you ever intentionally tried to keep your weight very low, even if others have told you it’s too low or unhealthy?

I wouldn’t say I’m trying to keep it “very low,” exactly… that sounds rather deliberate, doesn’t it?

But on workshop days, I suppose I do keep things pretty limited. I’ll usually just have tea, and maybe a few careful bites of something if I feel I should. Stopping for a proper meal feels unnecessary when I’m in the middle of work, and it sort of throws off the control I’ve got over the day.

I know that may not sound ideal. I’m not trying to be difficult about it.
Do you sometimes feel like your body looks bigger than it actually is, even when others tell you that you're very thin?

I don’t know that I’d say “bigger,” exactly. I mean, I hear people saying I’m very thin, and I’m not arguing with them.

It’s more that when I look at myself, I don’t always see what they seem to be seeing. Certain angles or clothes can make me feel… not quite comfortable, I suppose. But I don’t want to overstate it. I’m trying to answer properly.
Do you feel that your eating habits are mainly driven by a strong desire to control your shape or weight, more so than just feeling disciplined or focused on your work?

I suppose… yes, maybe more than I’d like to admit.

I try to tell myself it’s just discipline, or that I’m busy with work and don’t need much, but if I eat something heavy—or those holiday foods we used to make—I start worrying almost straight away that I’ll gain weight. Like I’ll lose the grip I’ve worked so hard to keep.

I know that probably sounds a bit much. I’m not trying to be unreasonable… but yes, it’s not only about being focused.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or any physical reasons why you might be eating less, like feeling full quickly or losing interest in food?

I wouldn’t say there’s a physical reason, exactly. I don’t think it’s that food suddenly doesn’t appeal to me.

It’s more on workshop days… I get into the work, and I’ll just have tea, maybe a few careful bites of something. Stopping for a real meal feels unnecessary, and honestly it throws off the control I feel like I’ve got over the day.

I know that may not be the sort of answer you mean, but that’s how it tends to happen.
When you look at yourself, do you feel that your body shape or weight influences how you see yourself overall, like whether you feel you're doing well or not in life?

I think it does, yes… though I’m a little embarrassed to say it that plainly.

If I’ve eaten something heavy, or let myself have the kind of holiday foods we used to make, I start worrying almost immediately that I’m going to gain weight. And then it feels like I’ve lost control, or lost the grip I’ve been trying so hard to keep.

So I suppose when I feel I’ve kept that grip, I feel like I’m doing better. I know that may not be a very balanced way to look at it.
